categories.name: NAND flash
categories.blurb: 3D NAND cells and process, reliability, page buffers and cache, ferroelectric NAND, QLC/PLC, and SSDs.

brief.idea: Charge-trap cells are stacked along a vertical channel hole, so density grows by adding word-line layers instead of shrinking the cell.
brief.why: Vendors have gone past 300 word-line layers and roadmaps aim at 400 and more, and AI data centres are buying high-capacity SSDs, so every extra layer and every thinner layer counts.
brief.industry: Samsung, SK hynix with Solidigm, Kioxia with SanDisk, Micron and YMTC compete on layer count, on bonding the CMOS wafer to the array wafer, and on QLC for AI storage.

brief.idea: Channel holes are etched through hundreds of oxide/nitride pairs in several decks, then the nitride is replaced by metal word lines.
brief.why: Thinner layers and taller stacks push etch aspect ratio, deck count, stress and word-line resistance to their limits.
brief.industry: Equipment makers push cryogenic high-aspect-ratio etch and molybdenum word lines in place of tungsten; memory makers trade deck count against cost per bit.

brief.idea: Threshold voltage drifts from charge loss, trap generation, disturb and lateral migration along the shared charge-trap layer.
brief.why: More bits per cell and thinner stacked layers shrink the margins, while AI and enterprise SSDs need stated endurance and retention.
brief.industry: Controllers lean on LDPC ECC, read retry and temperature-aware reads, and vendors qualify QLC drives for data-centre use.

brief.idea: Page buffers, sense amplifiers, cache latches and charge pumps move under or onto a bonded CMOS wafer so they cost no array area.
brief.why: I/O speed per die keeps rising and bonding the CMOS wafer separately frees the choice of peripheral transistor.
brief.industry: Vendors ship CMOS-under-array or CMOS-bonded-array designs and faster NAND interfaces each generation.

brief.idea: A ferroelectric hafnia gate stack stores the bit as polarisation instead of trapped charge, for lower program voltage and faster program.
brief.why: Low-voltage, low-power NAND matters for AI storage power budgets, and hafnia ferroelectrics are CMOS-friendly.
brief.industry: Memory makers and universities have shown ferroelectric vertical NAND strings at IEDM and VLSI; it is still research, not product.

brief.idea: Each cell holds 4 (QLC) or 5 (PLC) bits by placing more threshold-voltage levels in the same window.
brief.why: Cost per bit and drive capacity for AI data sets favour QLC, and PLC is the next step if margins allow.
brief.industry: Very high-capacity QLC enterprise SSDs (over 100 TB) are shipping for AI data centres, and PLC has been shown in prototypes.

brief.idea: The controller, flash translation layer, ECC and host interface turn raw NAND into a drive with the speed, endurance and latency the host needs.
brief.why: AI training and inference pipelines need storage that feeds GPUs fast, which drives PCIe 5/6 SSDs, new data-placement interfaces and CXL.
brief.industry: Vendors ship PCIe Gen5 drives and work on Gen6, and the NVMe group added flexible data placement for lower write amplification.

features.name: Data retention
features.tcad: Add trap-assisted charge loss: enable nonlocal tunneling and trap emission (Sentaurus Device: Traps with Tunneling, nonlocal path) and run a bake-temperature sweep.

features.name: P/E cycling endurance
features.tcad: Model interface/oxide trap generation versus cycles (trap generation rate tied to injected charge) and re-run Vt windows at 1k/3k/10k cycles.

features.name: Program & read disturb
features.tcad: Simulate the unselected string at Vpass/Vread with hot-carrier and FN injection models on, including the neighbouring word lines.

features.name: Cell-to-cell interference
features.tcad: Use a 3-cell (or 5-cell) string structure so charge in neighbours and lateral migration in the shared charge-trap layer is captured.

features.name: Temperature & cross-temperature
features.tcad: Turn on temperature-dependent mobility, trap emission and the poly-Si grain-boundary model, and sweep -40 °C to 125 °C.

features.name: Poly-Si channel grain boundaries
features.tcad: Add discrete grain boundaries with acceptor/donor trap densities in the poly-Si channel (randomised for variability).

features.name: Variability & statistics
features.tcad: Run a statistical (Monte Carlo) set: random dopants, grain-boundary positions and trap counts, then report Vt sigma.

features.name: Layer stacking & scaling
features.tcad: Extend the structure to the target layer count / pitch and check channel-hole taper and word-line resistance effects.

features.name: Cache program / page buffer
features.tcad: Device TCAD does not cover this; co-simulate the cell with a page-buffer netlist (see the circuit step).

features.name: CMOS under array
features.tcad: Add the thermal budget of the array process to the periphery transistors and check their drift.

features.name: Ferroelectric switching
features.tcad: Use a multi-domain ferroelectric model (e.g. Preisach / nucleation-limited switching) instead of a single-domain one.

features.name: ECC, sensing & ML read schemes
features.tcad: Generate Vt distributions from TCAD and feed them to an ECC / read-retry model to report raw bit error rate.

features.name: SSD / system-level evaluation
features.tcad: Not a TCAD effect: feed the device's Vt / error statistics into an SSD simulator (MQSim, FEMU) to show the system-level effect.

eda.compact_model: Verilog-A charge-trap cell model (Vt shift vs. program pulses, retention and disturb terms) fitted to the paper's data; BSIM4/BSIM-CMG for the select gates and periphery.
tools: Synopsys Sentaurus or Silvaco for TCAD-to-model extraction
steps: Extract a compact cell model from the device data (Vt vs. pulse count, Id-Vg, retention slope) and write it in Verilog-A.
Build a string of 4-8 cells plus select gates and a bit line with its real RC load.
Add a page buffer (sense latch, cache latch) and a simple ISPP program controller.
Simulate program, verify, read and cache-read timing; report tPROG, tR, energy per bit and the read margin.
Re-run with retention / disturb shifts applied to show how the device change affects bit errors.

tools: Silvaco Victory Process + Victory Device / Atlas
tcad.structure: One channel-hole string segment with 3 to 5 word lines, so the neighbouring cells are included: oxide core, poly-Si macaroni channel, tunnel oxide, Si3N4 charge-trap layer, blocking oxide, metal word lines. A 2D axisymmetric model is enough for one cell; use 3D for interference, lateral migration or hole-shape effects.
models: Drift-diffusion with doping- and field-dependent mobility
Nonlocal tunneling (Fowler-Nordheim and direct) through the tunnel oxide
Traps in the Si3N4 layer: energy, density and capture cross-section
Grain-boundary traps in the poly-Si channel
Hot-carrier injection, if the program scheme uses it
runs: Id-Vg before and after program and erase (gives Vt)
ISPP program and erase transients: Vt against pulse number
Retention bake: Vt shift against time at 85 to 150 °C
Endurance: Vt window after 1k, 3k and 10k P/E cycles
Disturb on the neighbouring cell and on an unselected string
tcad.calibrate: Before changing anything, reproduce measured Id-Vg and ISPP curves from a fabricated paper in this tree. A deck that does not match silicon will not convince a reviewer.
tcad.figure: Vt window, program speed (ISPP slope), retention loss and endurance

fab.route: A full 3D NAND stack needs an industrial line. In a university cleanroom, build a planar or few-layer vertical test cell (gate-all-around poly-Si channel with ONO), or work with an institute line such as imec or CEA-Leti.
tools: Synopsys Sentaurus (Sentaurus Process + Sentaurus Device) for the process flow
steps: Deposit the alternating SiO2/Si3N4 (or SiO2/poly-Si) layers by LPCVD or PECVD
Etch the channel hole by RIE, then deposit blocking oxide, nitride and tunnel oxide by ALD or LPCVD
Deposit and anneal the poly-Si channel, then fill the core oxide
Word-line metal (or gate replacement), contacts and a forming-gas anneal
measure: Id-Vg and Vt extraction (Keysight B1500A parameter analyzer (with pulse units))
Pulsed program and erase with ISPP
Retention bake at 85 to 150 °C, extrapolated with Arrhenius
P/E cycling to 10k cycles
Read and program disturb on neighbouring cells

categories.name: HBF, HBM & 3D memory
categories.blurb: High-bandwidth flash, HBM stacks, TSV and hybrid bonding, and CXL / processing-in-memory for AI.

brief.idea: Stack NAND dies with through-silicon vias, the way HBM stacks DRAM, beside the GPU: far more capacity than HBM, with read bandwidth good enough for model weights.
brief.why: AI inference models outgrow HBM capacity, and the weights are mostly read, which suits flash.
brief.industry: SanDisk introduced HBF in 2025 and signed an agreement with SK hynix to standardise it; first samples are talked about for 2026.

brief.idea: DRAM dies stacked with through-silicon vias on a base logic die, with a very wide interface on an interposer next to the processor.
brief.why: Every AI accelerator needs it, supply is tight, and each generation widens the interface and adds dies.
brief.industry: JEDEC published HBM4 with a 2048-bit interface in 2025; SK hynix, Samsung and Micron compete, and base dies move to foundry logic processes.

brief.idea: Dies or wafers are joined with TSVs, micro-bumps or direct copper-copper hybrid bonding to stack memory and logic.
brief.why: Taller HBM stacks under a fixed height limit, and NAND made from two bonded wafers, both push hybrid bonding.
brief.industry: Memory makers and equipment vendors develop hybrid bonding for future HBM, and wafer bonding is already used in NAND.

brief.idea: Move compute next to or into the memory, or share memory between processors over CXL, to beat the memory wall.
brief.why: AI workloads are limited by memory bandwidth and capacity more than by compute.
brief.industry: Memory makers have shown processing-in-memory DRAM and HBM parts, and CXL memory expanders are reaching servers.

features.name: Thermal in the stack
features.tcad: Build a thermal model of the full stack (dies, bonding layers, TIM) in COMSOL / Ansys Icepak and feed the temperatures back into the cell retention and refresh model.

features.name: TSV & bonding interconnect
features.tcad: Model TSV / bond parasitics and keep-out-zone stress on nearby transistors (process TCAD stress + 3D field solver).

features.name: Warpage & mechanical stress
features.tcad: Run a thermo-mechanical FEM of the stack and map the stress into mobility / Vt shifts of the cells.

features.name: Signal & power integrity
features.tcad: Extract channel S-parameters (HFSS / Sigrity) and simulate eye diagrams at the target data rate.

features.name: Read latency & bandwidth
features.tcad: Not a TCAD effect: model array timing (tR, tRCD) and channel count, then run it in a memory simulator.

features.name: Endurance & retention under AI workloads
features.tcad: Use measured or TCAD-derived retention / disturb models under read-heavy inference traffic.

features.name: Energy per bit
features.tcad: Break energy into array, I/O and TSV parts with circuit simulation and report pJ/bit.

features.name: ECC & RAS
features.tcad: Feed raw bit-error statistics into an ECC model and report uncorrectable error rate.

features.name: LLM / AI workload evaluation
features.tcad: Not a TCAD effect: run the memory model under an LLM inference trace (weights / KV cache) to show the benefit.

features.name: Processing in / near memory
features.tcad: Add the logic on the base die to the thermal and power budget.

features.name: CXL / memory pooling
features.tcad: Not a TCAD effect: evaluate in a system simulator with CXL latency added.

eda.compact_model: Behavioural models for the memory dies and I/O (IBIS-AMI / S-parameters for TSV channels), with cell timing and energy from circuit simulation.
tools: Cadence Sigrity / Ansys HFSS and SIwave (signal and power integrity)
Ramulator 2 / DRAMsim3 / gem5 (HBM and DRAM systems)
MQSim or FEMU (flash and HBF / SSD level)
Cadence Spectre / HSPICE (I/O and array circuits)
steps: Turn the device result into timing, energy and error-rate numbers per access.
Model the stack: channels, TSV / bonding parasitics, and the thermal path.
Run a memory-system simulator (Ramulator 2 / gem5 for HBM, MQSim for HBF) with an AI inference trace.
Report bandwidth, latency, energy per bit and temperature against an HBM or SSD baseline.

tools: Ansys Icepak / Mechanical or COMSOL Multiphysics (thermal and stress)
Synopsys Sentaurus Device or Silvaco Atlas for the memory cell
tcad.structure: The die stack: thinned dies, TSVs, micro-bumps or hybrid-bonding pads, underfill and the base logic die on an interposer. Add one memory cell or string at the hottest spot if the gap is about device behaviour.
models: Heat conduction with temperature-dependent conductivity and the real power map
Thermo-mechanical stress from CTE mismatch (keep-out zone, Cu pumping)
Electromigration current density in TSVs and bumps
Device level: mobility, leakage and retention against temperature and stress
runs: Steady and transient temperature maps under the real access pattern
Stress around TSVs and its effect on nearby transistors
Retention or read disturb of a cell at the hottest die
TSV channel signal integrity (S-parameters, eye diagram)
tcad.calibrate: Calibrate the stack's thermal resistance and warpage to a measured stack from a paper in this tree.
tcad.figure: peak temperature, stress, bandwidth per watt and retention at temperature

fab.route: Build test vehicles rather than products: daisy-chain TSV or hybrid-bonding structures, or stack commercial dies with a packaging partner.
tools: Packaging lab or partner (OSAT, institute line)
steps: TSV etch (Bosch DRIE), liner, barrier and seed, then Cu fill
Wafer thinning and backside reveal
Micro-bump or Cu-Cu hybrid bonding: surface activation, alignment, anneal
Underfill or molding and assembly on an interposer
measure: Daisy-chain and Kelvin contact resistance
Thermal resistance (thermal test die, IR camera)
Warpage and stress (shadow moire, Raman)
Eye diagram and bit error rate at the target data rate
Retention and refresh against temperature (DRAM) or read disturb (flash)

categories.name: DRAM
categories.blurb: DRAM cells and capacitors, 4F² and 3D DRAM, capacitorless gain cells, retention and row hammer, periphery and interfaces.

brief.idea: One transistor and one capacitor per bit, with a buried word-line access transistor and a tall high-k capacitor.
brief.why: Scaling below the current 10 nm-class nodes is hard: capacitor height, leakage and access-transistor drive all hit limits.
brief.industry: Vendors ship 1b and 1c nm-class nodes with EUV on more layers and look at new cell structures for the next steps.

brief.idea: A vertical channel transistor under the capacitor shrinks the cell from 6F² to 4F².
brief.why: It is the next density step on DRAM roadmaps once planar 6F² stops scaling.
brief.industry: Memory makers have shown vertical-channel DRAM cells in research and put 4F² on their roadmaps for the end of the decade.

brief.idea: Stack DRAM cells in layers like 3D NAND, or use capacitorless gain cells built from oxide semiconductors such as IGZO.
brief.why: Planar DRAM scaling is ending, so stacking is the long-term path to more bits per chip.
brief.industry: Memory makers and research labs such as imec show stacked-cell and IGZO 2T0C designs; nothing is in production yet.

brief.idea: Retention is limited by junction leakage and GIDL; row hammer flips bits when a nearby word line is opened many times.
brief.why: Smaller cells make row hammer worse and retention tighter, and it is a security issue as well as a reliability one.
brief.industry: JEDEC added refresh management and per-row activation counting to DDR5, and vendors add on-die mitigation.

brief.idea: Sense amplifiers, periphery transistors and I/O set DRAM speed and power.
brief.why: LPDDR and DDR speeds keep rising for AI phones, PCs and servers, which pushes the periphery toward high-k metal gate.
brief.industry: LPDDR5X is shipping and LPDDR6 is coming; vendors move periphery to HKMG.

features.name: Retention & leakage
features.tcad: Turn on band-to-band and trap-assisted tunneling (Hurkx / nonlocal BTBT) at the storage-node junction and compute retention time from leakage.

features.name: GIDL
features.tcad: Enable nonlocal band-to-band tunneling with calibrated parameters and sweep word-line negative bias.

features.name: Row hammer / row press
features.tcad: Simulate two neighbouring cells with transient aggressor word-line toggling and trap capture/emission at the STI and gate edge.

features.name: Variable retention time & traps
features.tcad: Add individual traps with capture/emission time constants near the junction and run a statistical set.

features.name: Temperature
features.tcad: Sweep temperature with temperature-dependent tunneling and SRH lifetimes on.

features.name: Variability
features.tcad: Run Monte Carlo on random dopants, work-function grains and capacitor geometry.

features.name: Capacitor dielectric
features.tcad: Model the capacitor stack with its real permittivity and leakage (Poole-Frenkel / TAT) instead of an ideal capacitor.

features.name: Oxide semiconductor channel (IGZO)
features.tcad: Use a density-of-states (tail + deep states) model for the amorphous oxide channel and its oxygen-vacancy donors.

features.name: Vertical / 3D stacking
features.tcad: Build the vertical or stacked structure in 3D and check floating-body and coupling effects between layers.

features.name: Gain cell (2T0C / 3T)
features.tcad: Co-simulate read and write transistors and the storage node charge in mixed-mode TCAD.

features.name: Sense margin & sensing scheme
features.tcad: Mixed-mode simulation of the cell plus the bit line and a sense amplifier.

eda.compact_model: BSIM4 / BSIM-CMG access transistor (or an RPI / oxide-TFT model for IGZO) plus a leaky storage capacitor, fitted to the paper's I-V and retention data.
tools: CACTI / DRAMsim3 / Ramulator for array and system level
steps: Fit a compact model for the access device and the storage node leakage.
Build a sub-array: cells on a bit line with the real bit-line capacitance, plus a latch-type sense amplifier.
Simulate write, read, restore and refresh; report sense margin, tRCD/tRAS and retention at temperature.
Feed the timing and energy into CACTI or DRAMsim3 to show the system-level benefit.

tools: Silvaco Victory Process + Victory Device / Atlas
tcad.structure: The access transistor (buried-channel or saddle-fin; vertical channel for 4F²) with the storage capacitor, either lumped or as a full cylinder MIM capacitor. For capacitorless cells, the IGZO 2T0C gain cell.
models: Band-to-band and trap-assisted tunneling (GIDL and junction leakage)
SRH recombination with field enhancement (Hurkx model)
High-k capacitor dielectric leakage (Poole-Frenkel)
Doping and mobility models; for IGZO, a density of states with tail and deep states
runs: Id-Vg and off-state leakage against temperature
Write and read transients with the bit line and capacitor
Retention time (leakage at 85 °C)
Row hammer: toggle the aggressor word line, track the victim's charge
tcad.calibrate: Calibrate leakage and Id-Vg to a measured cell from a paper in this tree before changing the structure.
tcad.figure: retention time, on-current, sense margin and row-hammer threshold

fab.route: Full DRAM arrays need an industrial line. At university, build discrete access transistors and MIM capacitors, or low-temperature oxide-semiconductor (IGZO) cells.
steps: Isolation and buried word-line recess etch, gate oxide and metal gate
Junction implants and activation anneal
MIM capacitor: TiN / ZrO2-Al2O3-ZrO2 / TiN by ALD
For IGZO cells: sputter or ALD the IGZO, gate stack, anneal in O2
measure: Id-Vg, GIDL and junction leakage against temperature (Keysight B1500A parameter analyzer (with pulse units))
C-V and dielectric leakage of the capacitor
Retention time with pulsed write and read
Row hammer on a small array

categories.name: Emerging memory
categories.blurb: MRAM (STT / SOT), ReRAM, phase-change memory, FeFET and FeRAM, and compute-in-memory built on them.

brief.idea: A magnetic tunnel junction stores the bit in its magnetisation and spin torque switches it; STT for embedded memory, SOT for faster caches.
brief.why: Embedded flash does not scale to advanced logic nodes, and MRAM does.
brief.industry: Foundries offer embedded MRAM at 22 nm-class nodes and below for microcontrollers and automotive.

brief.idea: A conductive filament forms and breaks in an oxide, switching between low and high resistance.
brief.why: It is simple, CMOS-friendly embedded memory and a candidate for analog compute-in-memory.
brief.industry: Foundries offer embedded RRAM at 22 nm-class nodes, and IP companies license it.

brief.idea: A chalcogenide switches between amorphous (high resistance) and crystalline (low resistance) by heating.
brief.why: After standalone 3D XPoint ended, interest moved to embedded PCM and to analog in-memory computing.
brief.industry: Embedded PCM is offered for automotive microcontrollers, and research labs build analog AI chips on PCM.

brief.idea: Ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide stores the bit as polarisation, in a FeFET gate or a FeRAM capacitor.
brief.why: Hafnia is already in CMOS fabs, so ferroelectric memory can be dense, fast and non-volatile at advanced nodes.
brief.industry: Memory makers have shown hafnia ferroelectric DRAM-like memory, and foundries and labs work on embedded FeFET.

brief.idea: Store neural network weights as conductances in a crossbar and do the multiply-accumulate in place with Ohm's and Kirchhoff's laws.
brief.why: AI inference energy is dominated by moving weights, which compute-in-memory avoids.
brief.industry: Research labs and start-ups show analog and digital in-memory AI chips; products are early.

features.name: Retention
features.tcad: Add the retention mechanism: oxygen-vacancy diffusion (ReRAM), thermal stability factor Δ (MRAM), drift / recrystallisation (PCM), depolarisation (FeFET), and run a bake-temperature sweep.

features.name: Endurance
features.tcad: Model degradation versus cycles (defect generation, fatigue, MgO breakdown) and report the window at 10^6–10^12 cycles.

features.name: Device-to-device & cycle-to-cycle variability
features.tcad: Run a stochastic model (kinetic Monte Carlo filament, multi-domain ferroelectric, thermal-field LLG) and report sigma.

features.name: Switching speed & energy
features.tcad: Sweep pulse width and amplitude to map the switching probability and energy.

features.name: Temperature
features.tcad: Include temperature in the switching and retention models and sweep -40 °C to 125 °C.

features.name: Multi-level / analog states
features.tcad: Model intermediate states and their drift; report linearity and number of separable levels.

features.name: Wake-up, imprint & disturb
features.tcad: Add field cycling history (wake-up / imprint) or the half-selected cell disturb in the array.

features.name: Scaling
features.tcad: Repeat the simulation at the target node dimensions and check edge effects.

features.name: Selector / 1S1R & 1T1R arrays
features.tcad: Co-simulate the cell with its selector or access transistor in the array.

features.name: BEOL / CMOS integration
features.tcad: Check the thermal budget of the process against the CMOS below it.

features.name: Compute-in-memory / neural networks
features.tcad: Generate conductance statistics from the device model and feed them into a CIM simulator (NeuroSim).

eda.compact_model: A Verilog-A compact model fitted to the paper's data: Stanford / JART VCM models for ReRAM, an MTJ model (macrospin with thermal field) for MRAM, a PCM electro-thermal model, or a Preisach / multi-domain FeFET model.
steps: Fit a Verilog-A compact model including variability and retention / endurance terms.
Build a 1T1R / 1S1R sub-array with write drivers and a sense amplifier (or ADCs for compute-in-memory).
Simulate write / read / verify and report energy, latency and read margin.
Run NVSim / NVMain (memory) or NeuroSim (CIM accuracy on a real network) to show the system-level benefit.

tools: Synopsys Sentaurus (Sentaurus Process + Sentaurus Device) for the access transistor and FeFET gate
COMSOL Multiphysics or Applied Materials Ginestra (ReRAM filament, PCM thermal)
tcad.structure: The memory element with its access transistor or selector: an MTJ pillar, a ReRAM metal-oxide-metal stack, a PCM mushroom or confined cell, or a FeFET gate stack.
models: MTJ: LLG dynamics with spin-transfer or spin-orbit torque and a thermal field
ReRAM: oxygen-vacancy drift and diffusion with Joule heating
PCM: electro-thermal heating with crystallisation kinetics
FeFET: Preisach or multi-domain Landau-Khalatnikov ferroelectric with interface traps
runs: Switching current or voltage against pulse width
Retention (thermal stability, resistance drift) at 85 to 150 °C
Endurance cycling
Device-to-device variability (Monte Carlo)
Read disturb
tcad.calibrate: Calibrate switching and retention to measured devices from a paper in this tree.
tcad.figure: switching energy, speed, retention, endurance and variability

fab.route: Most of these stacks can be made in a university cleanroom on Si: crossbars, or 1T1R cells on a foundry transistor wafer.
tools: University cleanroom (sputter, ALD, lithography, ion-beam etch)
steps: Bottom electrode, then the active stack: CoFeB/MgO MTJ (sputter), HfOx or TaOx (ALD), GST (sputter) or HfZrO (ALD)
Pattern pillars or crossbars (e-beam or optical lithography, ion-beam etch)
Top electrode and passivation; anneal to crystallise HZO or set the MTJ anisotropy
Add an access transistor (1T1R) if sneak paths or currents matter
measure: DC I-V and pulsed switching (Keysight B1500A parameter analyzer (with pulse units) with fast pulse units)
Retention bake and resistance drift
Endurance to 1e6 cycles or more
Cycle-to-cycle and device-to-device variability
MRAM: TMR and switching probability in a field

categories.name: High-power devices
categories.blurb: IGBTs and silicon power MOSFETs, ruggedness and reliability, and power modules.

brief.idea: IGBTs use bipolar conductivity modulation for low on-state loss at high voltage; superjunction MOSFETs balance charge in the drift region.
brief.why: Silicon still ships most power devices, and it competes with SiC on cost in EVs, solar and drives.
brief.industry: Vendors keep improving trench-gate and reverse-conducting IGBTs and superjunction MOSFETs on 300 mm wafers.

brief.idea: A power device must survive short circuit, avalanche, cosmic rays, gate stress and thousands of thermal cycles.
brief.why: EVs and AI data-centre power supplies need long, stated lifetimes from newer devices such as SiC and GaN.
brief.industry: Automotive qualification (AEC-Q101, AQG 324) and data-centre reliability specs drive testing.

brief.idea: The package sets heat removal, parasitic inductance and lifetime; sintered silver, double-sided cooling and embedded dies improve them.
brief.why: Fast-switching SiC and GaN and dense AI data-centre power push packages to their limits.
brief.industry: Module makers adopt silver sintering, double-sided cooling and low-inductance layouts for EV inverters and server power.

features.name: Self-heating & thermal
features.tcad: Use the thermodynamic (lattice temperature) model with a realistic heatsink boundary instead of isothermal simulation.

features.name: Breakdown & field termination
features.tcad: Include the edge termination region in the structure and use impact ionisation (e.g. van Overstraeten) for breakdown.

features.name: Short-circuit robustness
features.tcad: Run a mixed-mode short-circuit transient with the thermal model and metal melting limits.

features.name: Avalanche / UIS
features.tcad: Simulate unclamped inductive switching in mixed mode and look for current filamentation.

features.name: Latch-up & parasitic BJT
features.tcad: Model the full cell including the parasitic thyristor path and sweep current density.

features.name: Switching transients & losses
features.tcad: Run mixed-mode double-pulse tests with realistic gate resistance and stray inductance.

features.name: High-temperature operation
features.tcad: Sweep temperature with temperature-dependent lifetime, mobility and impact ionisation.

features.name: Power cycling & lifetime
features.tcad: Couple electro-thermal results to an FEM thermo-mechanical model (e.g. COMSOL / ANSYS) for solder and bond-wire stress.

features.name: Packaging & parasitics
features.tcad: Extract package parasitics (Q3D / FastHenry) and include them in the mixed-mode circuit.

features.name: Gate drive & control
features.tcad: Replace the ideal gate source with a gate driver model in mixed mode.

eda.compact_model: Physics-based IGBT / MOSFET compact model (e.g. Hefner IGBT or a fitted BSIM / MOS level model with thermal network) fitted to the paper's static and switching data.
tools: PLECS or PSIM for converter-level loss and thermal
ANSYS Q3D or COMSOL for package parasitics and thermal
steps: Fit a compact model with a Foster/Cauer thermal network from the paper's I-V, C-V and switching curves.
Build a double-pulse test bench with the measured stray inductance and a real gate driver.
Put the device in a target converter (boost, half-bridge inverter) and compute losses and efficiency over load.
Run a mission-profile thermal simulation to estimate junction temperature swing and lifetime.

tools: Silvaco Victory Process + Victory Device / Atlas
tcad.structure: A half or full unit cell of the trench or planar MOSFET or IGBT with the real drift layer, field plates and edge termination; add the package thermal network for ruggedness work.
models: Avalanche impact ionisation (van Overstraeten or Okuto-Crowell)
Self-heating with lattice temperature (thermodynamic model)
SRH and Auger recombination with carrier lifetime
High-field mobility saturation and temperature dependence
runs: Breakdown voltage and specific on-resistance
Switching transients in a mixed-mode double-pulse circuit
Short-circuit and unclamped inductive switching with self-heating
Safe operating area
tcad.calibrate: Calibrate to the datasheet or measured I-V and switching curves of a device in this tree.
tcad.figure: breakdown voltage, on-resistance, switching loss and short-circuit withstand time

fab.route: Power device fabrication needs a power line. Many groups instead build test circuits around commercial or partner devices and study packaging and reliability.
tools: Partner power-device line, or commercial devices
steps: Epitaxial drift layer and body implants
Trench etch, gate oxide and poly gate
Source and emitter implants, contacts and metal
Backside processing and die attach into a test package
measure: Static I-V and breakdown (curve tracer, e.g. Keysight B1505A)
Double-pulse switching test
Short-circuit and UIS tests
Power cycling, HTRB and HTGB

categories.name: Wide-bandgap devices
categories.blurb: SiC MOSFETs, GaN HEMTs, vertical GaN, and ultra-wide-bandgap Ga₂O₃, AlN and diamond.

brief.idea: 4H-SiC has a wide bandgap and high critical field, so thin drift layers block high voltage with low loss.
brief.why: 800 V EV drivetrains, chargers and renewables use it, and 200 mm wafers and falling substrate prices widen its use.
brief.industry: Suppliers are moving to 200 mm wafers and new capacity, with Chinese makers growing fast and prices falling.

brief.idea: A two-dimensional electron gas at the AlGaN/GaN interface gives a fast, low-loss lateral switch.
brief.why: Chargers, data-centre power supplies and higher-voltage AI rack power need fast, efficient switches.
brief.industry: GaN-on-silicon is moving to 300 mm wafers, bidirectional GaN switches are appearing, and the foundry landscape is changing.

brief.idea: Current flows vertically through a thick GaN drift layer, so GaN can reach kilovolt ratings like SiC.
brief.why: It could bring GaN's speed to voltages lateral HEMTs cannot reach.
brief.industry: It is still mostly research and start-ups, limited by the cost of GaN substrates; GaN-on-silicon and engineered substrates are being tried.

brief.idea: Gallium oxide, AlN, AlGaN and diamond have bandgaps above 4.5 eV, for even higher breakdown fields than SiC and GaN.
brief.why: Gallium oxide substrates can be grown from the melt, which could make them cheap.
brief.industry: Gallium oxide start-ups and labs make diodes and transistors; the open problems are p-type doping and heat removal.

features.name: Self-heating & thermal
features.tcad: Turn on the lattice-temperature model with anisotropic thermal conductivity and the substrate / heat-spreader stack.

features.name: Trapping & current collapse
features.tcad: Add buffer (carbon / iron) and surface donor traps with their energy levels and run transient off-to-on switching.

features.name: Threshold instability (BTI)
features.tcad: Model border/interface traps in the gate oxide (e.g. a two-stage NMP model) and simulate stress/recovery.

features.name: Breakdown & field management
features.tcad: Include field plates / termination and use impact ionisation coefficients for the right polytype and orientation.

features.name: Gate oxide & interface
features.tcad: Add an interface-state density profile (Dit vs. energy) and mobility degradation at the interface.

features.name: High-temperature operation
features.tcad: Sweep temperature with temperature-dependent mobility, polarisation and trap emission.

features.name: Polarisation & 2DEG
features.tcad: Use the strain-dependent piezoelectric polarisation model and check 2DEG density versus barrier thickness.

features.name: Short-circuit & avalanche ruggedness
features.tcad: Run mixed-mode short-circuit / UIS transients with the thermal model on.

features.name: Normally-off (E-mode) gate
features.tcad: Model the p-GaN or recessed gate stack including the Schottky metal / p-GaN junction.

features.name: Monolithic integration & drivers
features.tcad: Simulate two devices on the same substrate to capture back-gating / substrate crosstalk.

features.name: RF / high-frequency
features.tcad: Run AC small-signal simulation to extract fT/fmax including parasitics.

eda.compact_model: ASM-HEMT or MVSG (GaN, CMC standard) / a SiC MOSFET compact model with thermal network, fitted to the paper's I-V, C-V and pulsed data; trapping as an extra sub-circuit.
tools: Cadence Spectre with the ASM-HEMT Verilog-A model
steps: Fit ASM-HEMT / MVSG (GaN) or a SiC MOSFET model to the measured DC, C-V and pulsed I-V; add dynamic Ron with a trap sub-circuit.
Build a double-pulse test bench with realistic layout parasitics and the gate driver the device needs.
Use the device in a target circuit: a totem-pole PFC / LLC / half-bridge inverter for power, or a PA in ADS for RF.
Report efficiency, switching loss, ringing and junction temperature versus Si or SiC baselines.

tools: Silvaco Victory Process + Victory Device / Atlas
tcad.structure: SiC: a MOSFET half-cell with the SiO2/SiC interface. GaN: the AlGaN/GaN heterostructure with buffer, field plates and p-GaN gate. Ga2O3: the lateral or vertical device with its substrate.
models: Polarisation charge at the AlGaN/GaN interface (GaN)
Interface and buffer traps (Dit, carbon-doped buffer)
Incomplete ionisation of dopants (SiC, Ga2O3)
Anisotropic mobility (4H-SiC) and impact ionisation
Self-heating with the real thermal conductivity (important for Ga2O3)
runs: Id-Vg, Id-Vd and breakdown
Dynamic on-resistance and current collapse after off-state stress
Threshold drift under gate bias
Switching in a mixed-mode double-pulse circuit
Temperature map at rated power
tcad.calibrate: Calibrate traps and mobility to measured I-V and pulsed I-V from a device in this tree.
tcad.figure: breakdown voltage, on-resistance, dynamic Ron, threshold stability and switching loss

fab.route: GaN-on-Si and Ga2O3 devices can be made in a university cleanroom on bought epi wafers; SiC MOSFETs usually need a partner line for implants and high-temperature anneals.
tools: University cleanroom with bought epi wafers, or a partner line
steps: Mesa isolation or implant isolation
Ohmic contacts (Ti/Al/Ni/Au for GaN) with rapid thermal anneal
Gate dielectric (ALD Al2O3 or SiO2) or p-GaN gate, then gate metal
Field plates, passivation (SiN) and pads
measure: Static I-V and breakdown
Pulsed I-V for trapping and dynamic Ron
Gate-bias stress (HTGB) and Vth drift
Double-pulse switching
Raman thermography or thermoreflectance for self-heating
